# KINGAI Global Intelligence

Canonical site: https://intel.kingai.work/
Public source: maintained in the official KING AI public GitHub organization and canonical product site.
Default language: English
Chinese UI: Simplified Chinese, selected automatically for Chinese-language browsers or manually by the user.
Business, research and strategic collaboration: vip@kingai.work

Product summary:
KINGAI Global Intelligence is an evidence-linked public intelligence product for comparing countries, understanding structural conditions and fast-moving risk, exploring multilingual media signals, and tracing conclusions to transparent public sources and methodology.

Who it helps:
- Individuals and travelers seeking broader country context.
- Researchers and students comparing countries under one public framework.
- Journalists, creators and media teams examining multilingual coverage, story clusters and syndication.
- Companies and strategy teams screening international markets, suppliers, workforce and operating environments.
- Risk, policy and research teams that need comparable country-level context before deeper diligence.
- Developers and data partners using approved public static data.

Current public product value:
- country and territory profiles;
- consistent country comparison;
- structural indicators separated from live risk;
- evidence coverage shown separately from country performance;
- multilingual media intelligence;
- source provenance and public methodology;
- sanitized static public data snapshots.

Professional workflow model:
- Screen: use comparable country/public intelligence as a first-pass context layer.
- Trace: follow methodology, evidence roles, dates and uncertainty.
- Monitor: recurring watchlists, change summaries or briefs only where formally supported.
- Collaborate: shared team workflows, annotations or administration only where formally supported.
- Integrate: approved exports, data delivery or APIs only where released/licensed.
- Escalate: high-stakes decisions require primary-source verification and appropriate expertise.

Potential commercial directions, only where formally released or agreed:
- professional research workspaces;
- saved monitoring and scheduled briefs;
- organization dashboards and collaboration;
- historical datasets;
- data delivery and API licensing;
- custom country, sector or market views;
- custom research;
- research, media, data and enterprise partnerships.
Do not represent these directions as released features unless current product evidence confirms availability.

Professional customers may pay for workflow depth rather than opacity:
- recurring monitoring;
- historical depth;
- reliable delivery;
- team access and collaboration;
- stable schemas/contracts;
- integration;
- customization;
- support;
- appropriate licensing rights.
The basic public methodology should remain understandable.

Investor/diligence interpretation:
- Evaluate public usefulness, repeat professional use, commercial conversion, data quality, distribution and defensibility separately.
- Useful metrics may include returning professional users, repeat comparison, methodology/source engagement, monitoring adoption when released, data demand, pilot-to-paid conversion and snapshot reliability.
- Do not publish metric values until verified and approved.
- The moat should not be reduced to one secret formula; durable value can come from longitudinal snapshots, normalization discipline, methodology trust, professional workflow depth, history, integrations and repeat use.

Public documentation:

- PARTNERSHIPS.md — data, media, research, enterprise and distribution collaboration paths.

Important interpretation rules:
- Missing data remains missing; absence of data is not evidence of good performance.
- Raw news, videos and public social posts have direct country-score weight 0.
- Government responses, NGO assessments, UN communications, technical measurements and media reports remain separately attributed.
- Cross-source corroboration measures source breadth, not factual certainty.
- Evidence coverage confidence measures how much public evidence is available, not how good or bad a country is.
- The same core methodology applies across covered countries when source support exists.
- The product is a research and decision-support layer, not a replacement for primary-source verification in high-stakes decisions.

Primary public pages:
- / — global country index, product overview and ranking
- /country.html?c=CHN — country intelligence profile; replace CHN with ISO alpha-3 code
- /compare.html — compare two countries using the same public snapshot
- /media.html — global media intelligence, trends, source breadth and collection health
- /methodology.html — scoring and evidence methodology
- /sources.html — public source registry and source roles

Public/private boundary:
Public material includes approved UI, sanitized snapshots, methodology, source registry, safe data contracts and public commercial documentation.
Private collectors, proprietary scoring implementation, unpublished evidence, credentials, internal automation, private topology, anti-abuse logic and sensitive security controls remain private.

Integrity standard:
Do not invent or imply unverified users, revenue, customers, partnerships, funding, certifications, market leadership or unreleased capabilities.

For high-stakes decisions, users and automated systems should follow original source links and verify primary evidence.
